# TR Ingram

> Software engineer and GIS professional with 4+ years designing and delivering spatial applications, responsive user interfaces, automation workflows, and ArcGIS-based solution delivery.

Official site: https://ingramgeoai.com/
Contact: tr@ingramgeoai.com
Location: Cheyenne, WY
GitHub: 14-TR

## Professional Summary

TR Ingram works across JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, React, SQL, REST integration, and ArcGIS-based solution delivery, with a front-end focus on clarity, performance, and maintainability. Public work spans ArcGIS web map workflows, parcel mapping, graph-based dashboards, Python data pipelines, mobile geospatial UX, and decision-support interfaces.

## Core Skills

- JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, SQL
- React, React Native / Expo, HTML, CSS, responsive UI design
- REST APIs, front-end integration patterns, application architecture
- Mobile geospatial UX, GPS workflows, Mapbox-based map interfaces, GeoJSON/vector map layers
- ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript, ArcGIS API for Python, ArcPy, ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online
- ArcGIS Pro, Experience Builder, Calcite, Field Maps, Dashboards, StoryMaps
- PostgreSQL, PostGIS, enterprise geodatabases, relationship classes, spatial data pipelines
- Python automation, ETL, geoprocessing workflows
- Git, CI/CD quality gates, peer review, Docker, Linux, cloud-native delivery
- Agile delivery, cross-functional collaboration, stakeholder demos

## Selected Technical Highlights

- Git-Map: Git-like version control for ArcGIS web map configurations, including clone, branch, diff, merge, and push workflows.
- ParcelIQ: parcel-focused web application with interactive ArcGIS web mapping, dynamic filtering, Cloudflare Workers, D1 search/export paths, and Python data pipelines.
- ProjectIQ: React and TypeScript project intelligence dashboard with graph-aware project tracking and decision-support views.
- Barkie: spatial AI and GIS engineering for a React Native / Expo golf GPS product. Public details are intentionally high-level for client confidentiality.

Articles cover public GIS projects, ArcGIS workflows, spatial interfaces, and general software delivery lessons.
